label: Copy phase, late position: copying among x/i/m/l (e.g. x->i, m->i, i->l)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during the original tokens or on <DEL>), mostly at recall_idx 3-6 (peak at 4) and never at recall_idx 0-1. Input token is nearly always x, i, m or l (93% of mass), and it is strongest when the output is i or l, i.e. when copying bigrams such as x->i, m->i, i->l, i->i. The top activations (up to 4.9) are on x or m right before an i (e.g. ...x i i..., ...t m i l...). Never fires on the first occurrence of a token (in_first=0 at every active step), which follows from its being copy-phase only. Input x by itself fires weakly with other outputs (x->o, x->r), and the same token pairs early in the copy (recall_idx<3) give little or no activation. Precision is limited because many late-position x/i/m/l steps stay silent for reasons this predicate does not capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: x, i, m, l, o, h; least: j, u, b, e) and the token being output (most: i, l, x, m, h, v; least: t, -, k, e); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=3, recall_idx=5.
